Lamborghini Temerario Spyder: Is It the Go-To Open-Top Supercar of the Moment?
8 photos
Photo: Lamborghini
Imagine this: you just hit the jackpot or inherited a huge amount of money and you want an open-top supercar. Which model do you choose?
Well, there are quite a few models to choose from. Porsche’s 911 Turbo S Cabriolet is more of a daily driver. Ferrari’s 296 GTS is definitely on the list, and so are the Artura Spider and 750S Spider from McLaren. There is also a newcomer to the segment. It’s the Raging Bull’s new open-top “baby” supercar, which adds the Spyder suffix to the Temerario.
We knew it was coming even before Lamborghini pulled the wraps off the Temerario more than two years ago. That’s because its predecessors, including the Huracan and the Gallardo, were all offered in this configuration, in addition to the fixed-roof body styles, and over the years, the convertible variants came in all kinds of different configurations, some of which were more track-focused than others.
Therefore, it was not exactly a surprise when we saw the first prototypes of the new open-top Lambo earlier this year doing their thing in the open, with their bodies fully wrapped in camouflage to the point where it was almost impossible to catch a decent glimpse at the thing that separates it from the regular model. That would be the folding hardtop, which represents a major step up from the rag top of its predecessors.
This is the company’s first-ever retractable hardtop supercar, and while some might argue that a folding fabric roof would have lowered the center of gravity, while also keeping the weight in check, others would say that this is the best possible choice for such a thing. By the way, let’s not forget that models such as the Aventador Roadster and the Diablo VT roadster featured split panels, though they had to be manually removed and stowed.
Photo: Lamborghini When it comes to the Lamborghini Temerario Spyder, the roof lowers and raises at the push of a button. This component features ten electric actuators and not an electro-hydraulic system, which would have been the more traditional approach. And it is definitely worth noting that the Artura Spider and the 296 GTS from McLaren and Ferrari, respectively, also benefit from hardtops.
Lamborghini’s new Temerario Spyder has a dry weight of 3,979 pounds (1,805 kg), and that makes it exactly 220 pounds (100 kg) heavier than its fixed roof sibling, which tips the scale at 3,759 lbs (1,705 kg( dry. The front-to-rear weight distribution has changed from 43.4% front - 56.6% rear to 43.2% front - 56.8% rear, the spec sheet reveals. As for the total length, width, and height, these remain the same, and so does the space between the axles.
Another thing that hasn’t changed is the plug-in hybrid powertrain. The 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine, which can be revved all the way up to 10,000 rpm, still develops 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) between 9,000 and 9,750 rpm. The V8 is assisted by three axial-flux electric motors, and the total system output is 907 hp (920 ps/677 kW). From 0 to 62 mph (0-100 kph), the Temerario Spyder needs 2.8 seconds, which is 0.1 seconds slower than the Temerario Coupe, and at 213 mph (343 kph), the top speed is the same.
A carry-over aluminum spaceframe chassis, carbon ceramic brakes, a retuned suspension compared to its fixed-roof sibling , an eight-speed automatic transmission, all-wheel drive, an aluminum body, 9x20-inch wheels at the front and 11.5x21-inch wheels at the rear, and others are thing, including the front and rear damping system (Lamborghini MagneRide), and the front and rear double wishbone suspension.
Photo: Lamborghini The Lamborghini Temerario Spyder also benefits from a three-level neck warmer in order to keep the occupants warm in cold temperatures. There is also a power-operated rear window that allows the cockpit to be bathed in the exhaust sound when it is lowered, even with the roof raised. The Raging Bull says that the model can accommodate individuals up to 6 feet and 7 inches (2 meters) tall, and that makes it more spacious than the demised Huracan Evo Spyder.
In addition to the open-top design, complete with the special compartment behind the seats, the Lamborghini Temerario Spyder sets itself apart from the Temerario Coupe by featuring hexagonal cowls behind the headrests. Interested parties can choose from a plethora of paint finishes for the exterior and interior colors, and those numbers further increase if you bring Ad Personam, which is Lambo’s personalization division, into discussion.
Before wrapping things up, we have to remind you that the Temerario Spyder is not the first open-top Lambo from the company’s new-age lineup, because that model would be the rare Fenomeno Roadster . However, the latter does not feature a retractable hardtop, a soft top, a targa design, nor a removable panel, as it is permanently open. Production is capped at 15 units in this case, whereas its fixed-roof variant is limited to 29 examples. And this makes the Fenomeno a “few-off” supercar.
It is only a matter of time until Lamborghini introduces the Revuelto Roadster, and it will be interesting to see what path it will choose for the roof. Still, if we had to guess, we’d say that probably a manually-removable one.
Meanwhile, if you had deep pockets (or maybe you do), and wanted to spruce up your weekend (or perhaps daily) drives with a modern-day convertible supercar, would you pick the new Lamborghini Temerario Spyder ? I know I would, but then again, I’ve always been a Lambo fan!
